newsitem.title: USA: MSRB agrees to no rule G-37 changes at PSA meeting.
newsitem.headline: MSRB agrees to no rule G-37 changes at PSA meeting.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board agreed to make no revisions to the board's "pay-to-play" rule during a three-hour meeting with 20 representatives of municipal bond firms on Thursday, an industry spokesman said.

PSA The Bond Market Trade Association had requested the meeting last month after dealers complained about several provisions of MSRB's April 1994 rule G-37, which bars muni dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
"It was a great meeting," said PSA senior vice president Joseph Sack in a telephone interview following the meeting at PSA headquarters here.
Dealers told MSRB staff members that the rule seems unduly harsh in some places, but they made no formal requests for revision, Sack and MSRB executive director Christopher Taylor said.
"They didn't ask us to make any changes so we didn't agree to make any," Taylor said in a telephone interview.
Sack said dealers were concerned that a firm could be banned from doing business with a locality under G-37 even if an employee inadvertently gave as little as $50 to a municipal official.
MSRB staff conceded that the provision is a tough one but that the board has a strong interest in protecting the reputation of the muni bond industry, Sack said.

Sack said dealers also were worried about how to guard against a G-37 violation when they give to a political action committee. The concern is that a PAC could steer dollars to a specific municipal candidate without their knowledge, Sack said.

Taylor said, in response, he reminded dealers that they can protect themselves by sending a letter along with the donation saying it is their understanding that the money will be distributed to a range of candidates, not just one or two.
Sack said, "The key to G-37 is that the way you can prove you are in the right is to have sound written supervisory procedures and demonstrate that you follow them."
He said MSRB's staff urged firms to have sound written procedures for complying with G-37 and to demonstrate that you follow them.
Sack said the "consensus" of industry participants following Thursday's meeting was that MSRB staff was "reasonable."
